samples.question: This page shows black ink together with coloured decorations in red, blue, orange, purple, green and grey. Only black ink counts as a wall; coloured and grey marks never count, even when a decoration is drawn as a closed ring with its own hole. A white area is shut in when you cannot travel from it to the edge of the page without crossing black ink, and its depth is the number of separate black rings you must cross to get out. A black ring that carries a visible gap is not a wall around anything: you may walk through the gap, however narrow it looks and however far it lies from the area you started in. Exactly two clusters of black rings on this page shut in a white core; each of those clusters is a stack of two or three black square rings drawn one inside the other around its own core, and the two clusters stand apart with plain white page between them. Every other black mark on the page shuts in nothing. The two cores never have the same depth: one is shut in by exactly one more unbroken ring than the other. How large a cluster is, how many rings are drawn in it, how much black ink it holds, where on the page the pair sits, and how many coloured marks are drawn never decide the answer. Taking the two clusters in left-to-right order, which cluster's core is shut in by more unbroken black rings? Answer left or right.
